 Abhilash Botekar / Nov 15, 2026, 22:28 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print Nashik’s maximum temperature fell from 34°C to a season-low 31.6°C on Sunday Nashik : Outpacing even the famed hill station of Mahabaleshwar, Nashik emerged as the coolest among the major cities monitored by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) across Maharashtra on Sunday morning, recording a minimum temperature of 12.6°C. The city shed 0.8 degrees compared to Saturday and outchilled Mahabaleshwar in Satara district, which settled at 14.6°C. Temperatures across most other cities in the state hovered around the 14-degree mark. The IMD observatory in Nashik has been registering a steady downward slide in the mercury over the past four days, bringing a crisp wintry nip to the air. Weather officials confirmed that the chill is here to stay for the next few days, prompting residents to bundle up in woollens while others celebrated the dip with cold treats. “Since Nov 5, when the minimum temperature was recorded at 18.4°C, the mercury has dropped to 12.6°C on Nov 15. This is 2.7 degrees lower than the normal temperatures recorded during this time. This is likely to remain in the range of 12 to 13°C for several more days,” an IMD official said. Nashik’s maximum temperature fell from 34°C to a season-low 31.6°C on Sunday amid considerable daytime cooling over 10 days. “It is still 1.4 degrees higher than the normal temperature,” an IMD official said. Elsewhere in the district, Niphad town — known for consistently recording lower temperatures than Nashik city — dipped even further to 11.5°C, according to data from the agriculture research centre of Rahuri Agricultural University. The winter chill extended across neighbouring districts as well. Jalgaon witnessed a drop to 13°C, which is 2.3 degrees below its average temperature. Meanwhile, Ahilyanagar recorded a minimum of 14.3°C and Pune settled at 13.5°C, marking a dip of 1.9 degrees below normal. Pune’s daytime weather remained more comfortable than Nashik’s, with its maximum temperature settling at 30.4°C. The sudden onset of winter has brought a welcome change for Nashik residents, although chilly mornings pose minor challenges for parents. Join conversation

 “The dry and cold nights have forced Nashikites to pull out the woolens from the closets. The sweaters, the blankets and the others that have been resting a while are now out,” homemaker Shambhavi Sonar said. Sonar said she enjoyed the pleasant weather but struggled to get her two children, aged 13 and 9, out of bed in the mornings. On the flip side, a section of residents is embracing the dip in mercury by indulging in cold desserts. “The pleasure of eating a scoop is just an out of the world experience,” said Suyog Gharat, a resident of Gangapur Road.
